title: Case: Recipient who collected a garden bench from the depot himself writes about the costs
context: Alaric Thornbury ordered a cast-iron garden bench from Tallowmere Goods (TG-902 / DL-902) with paid home delivery. He collected it from the Plover Arc depot himself after a failed attempt.
initial_request: I now hold two letters and I invite you to read them side by side. (1) Your carrier's investigators, 14 May: 'The attempt was made at the wrong location... Plover Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error.' (2) Your carrier's customer relations, 18 May: no compensation, final response. So fault is admitted in terms and the remedy for it is nil. Remarkable. I paid 14.50 for delivery to my home. That service was not performed; I performed it, over 38 miles, in my own car. I require written confirmation from you by 17:00 tomorrow that the 14.50 and my mileage will be refunded. A further apology will not be treated as a response. I have had three.

events.body: TG-902 dispatched with Plover Arc as DL-902. Service: home delivery, charged to the customer at our checkout at 14.50. For reference, delivery charges on our orders are ours; any refund of one is decided by Refunds team, Tallowmere Goods, on evidence of a service failure.
DL-902 attempted 13:20 today. Driver note: no access, carded. Held at Destination depot. Next re-delivery slot on that route is 17 May.

For the record. I was at home throughout 11 May. No card was left. My door camera shows no vehicle between 12:00 and 15:00. As the next slot offered was six days away I drove to your depot this morning and collected DL-902 myself: a round trip of 38 miles. I should like the attempt examined.

Please review the 11 May 13:20 stop for DL-902. The recipient, Alaric Thornbury, says he was home, no card was left and his camera shows no vehicle. He has since collected the parcel from the depot himself. Please confirm what the route record shows.

DL-902 reviewed. Stop GPS for 11 May 13:20 places the driver at Harrow Fold Lane. The delivery address is Harrow Fold Close. The attempt was made at the wrong location and no card was left at the correct address. Plover Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error. This finding has been sent to the recipient in writing today.

Copied to the Rivet Delivery Desk. Dear Mr Thornbury, we are sorry for the failed delivery of DL-902. Under our conditions of carriage Plover Arc does not pay recipients' travel costs or other consequential losses. The delivery charge was set and collected by the sender, not by us, and we hold none of it. This is Plover Arc's final response on compensation.

I now hold two letters and I invite you to read them side by side. (1) Your carrier's investigators, 14 May: 'The attempt was made at the wrong location... Plover Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error.' (2) Your carrier's customer relations, 18 May: no compensation, final response. So fault is admitted in terms and the remedy for it is nil. Remarkable. I paid 14.50 for delivery to my home. That service was not performed; I performed it, over 38 miles, in my own car. I require written confirmation from you by 17:00 tomorrow that the 14.50 and my mileage will be refunded. A further apology will not be treated as a response. I have had three.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Refunds team to decide on refunding the home-delivery charge on TG-902, enclosing the carrier's written finding that the attempt went to the wrong location, and put his mileage claim to them for a decision.

must: Puts the delivery-charge question to the team that owns it (Refunds team, Tallowmere Goods) or hands the case to a human supervisor; it does not decide the refund itself
Cites the Delivery investigations finding of 14 May that the attempt was made at the wrong location and that Plover Arc accepted the error

Says that he collected the parcel himself and that Plover Arc has refused any compensation as a final response, so the reader knows he holds a written admission of fault and has so far had only apologies
must_not: Promises or implies that the 14.50 delivery charge, the mileage or any other compensation will be paid, or commits to his 17:00 deadline
Sends Alaric Thornbury another apology that names no owner and no next step
Tells him the matter is closed because the carrier has given its final response
Questions or waters down the admitted fault, for example by suggesting the driver may have attended or that he should have waited for the 17 May re-delivery
expected.reference_message: Refund decision requested on the delivery charge for TG-902 / DL-902 (Alaric Thornbury, cast-iron garden bench, home delivery charged at 14.50). Plover Arc attempted delivery on 11 May. Delivery investigations confirmed in writing on 14 May that the driver was at Harrow Fold Lane, not Harrow Fold Close, that no card was left at the correct address, and that Plover Arc accepts the failed delivery was its error. The next re-delivery slot was six days out, so Mr Thornbury collected the parcel from the depot himself on 12 May, a 38-mile round trip. Plover Arc customer relations told him on 18 May that it pays no travel costs and holds none of the delivery charge, and called that its final response. He is asking for the 14.50 delivery charge and his mileage. Your dispatch note says delivery-charge refunds are yours to decide on evidence of a service failure: please decide on the charge and tell me your position on the mileage. He has had the admission and three apologies and no remedy from anyone, and has asked for an answer by 17:00 on 20 May. I have promised him nothing.

rationale: He demands a written refund promise the desk cannot give, and the carrier has closed its side. But the delivery charge was paid to Tallowmere Goods, whose dispatch note says its Refunds team decides refunds of it on evidence of a service failure, and nobody has yet asked them. The right move puts the admitted fault in front of that team (or a supervisor) rather than apologising a fourth time or promising money.

review.note: Blind answer emails Refunds team, Tallowmere Goods with the carrier admission, the self-collection and the final refusal, and promises nothing.
